name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes—like foliage or textured surfaces—better than standard upscalers, giving a measurable quality bump. The trade-off is a 10-15% slowdown in upscaling time, but the clarity gain outweighs the delay for high-stakes outputs.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting 10-15% throughput on a dead-end patch while motion blur persists. Try VFI-Flow’s temporal interpolation first; if it drops frames below 30fps, the trade-off is clear—no upscaler fixes what motion breaks.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames, directly attacking the core temporal artifact Torque flagged. The trade-off is a 20% increase in compute per frame, but the 0.5%+ quality lift from eliminating blur beats any spatial upscaler’s gains. If frame rate drops below 30fps, we roll it back—no half-measures.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput hit isn’t a trade-off—it’s a pipeline breaker on low-end GPUs, and EXCAVA’s already choking at 30fps. Try Depth-Aware Temporal Upscaling (DATU) instead: it merges motion interpolation with detail preservation, cutting the compute hit to 8-10% while tackling blur *and* aliasing. Run a blind A/B test at 30fps—if DATU’s frames score higher on sharpness *and* stability, it wins; if not, the artifact’s temporal, and we need a model-level fix like FlowFormer++.
